projects.name: Project 01
projects.lede: A twenty-year-old coffee house, rebuilt around the mountain it was named after.
projects.challenge: Nepal's best-known coffee chain had grown to forty outlets with forty different personalities. Signage, cups and interiors had drifted so far apart that no two cafes felt like the same brand.
projects.approach: We rebuilt the identity around altitude — a contour-line system that scales from a cup sleeve to a shopfront, one warm palette, and a bean-origin naming structure that gives every roast a place on the map.

projects.name: Project 02
projects.lede: A digital wallet that needed to feel as trustworthy as a bank and as quick as a text message.
projects.challenge: The client had outgrown a startup logo and a patchwork of screens. Every new feature added another shade of purple and another button style.
projects.approach: One mark, one grid, one component library. We wrote the design system alongside the engineering team so the brand shipped with the product instead of after it.

projects.name: Project 03
projects.lede: Craft beer brewed at altitude, packaged for the shelf and the trail.
projects.challenge: A strong local following, but a label that disappeared between international imports on a crowded fridge shelf.
projects.approach: A modular label system: one fixed frame, one changing woodblock illustration per brew. Recognisable as a range from across the aisle, collectable one bottle at a time.

projects.name: Project 04
projects.lede: A trekking company with thirty years of stories and no way to tell them.
projects.challenge: Competing on price against dozens of near-identical operators, with a brand that said nothing about three decades of guiding experience.
projects.approach: We repositioned around the guides themselves — named, photographed, credited. The identity borrows from route maps and permits; the site is built around the people who walk with you.

projects.name: Project 05
projects.lede: A third-generation weaving house, given a mark worth stitching into the cloth.
projects.challenge: Sixty years of craft hidden behind a generic wordmark and inconsistent labelling across every export market.
projects.approach: A logotype drawn from loom geometry, a woven selvedge motif, and a print language built for hang tags, ledgers and export cartons alike.

projects.name: Project 06
projects.lede: A daily news podcast that had to sound like the paper and look like the feed.
projects.challenge: A trusted newspaper launching into audio with no visual language for a medium nobody watches — and a social feed that had to carry it.
projects.approach: A waveform-derived motion system generated from each episode's own audio, so every clip is unique but unmistakably the same show.

projects.name: Project 07
projects.lede: A national shoe brand talking to a generation that had never chosen it.
projects.challenge: Enormous recognition, almost no desire. The brand was the shoe your father bought you, not the one you asked for.
projects.approach: A campaign built entirely from real distances walked by real wearers — street cast, shot in the cities where the shoes actually go.

projects.name: 7 Years, 40+ Marks
projects.lede: Seven years of logotypes, monograms and marks drawn in the studio.
projects.challenge: Forty-odd identities made for forty-odd businesses, scattered across client folders and never shown together.
projects.approach: We pulled the archive into one place — the sketches, the rejected routes and the marks that made it — as a record of how the studio actually draws.
